sentences.text: Erlikosaurus possessed a well-developed beak and toothed jaws adapted for a herbivorous diet. It had four toes on its feet, with the first toe articulated to the ankle. The animal also had a large gut, strong arms with elongated claws, and a pelvis directed backwards. It is known for having the most complete skull among therizinosaurids from the Bayan Shireh Formation.
CT scans of the holotype skull revealed that Erlikosaurus had well-developed senses of smell, hearing, and balance.
The name Erlikosaurus combines the Turko-Mongolian demon king Erlik with the Greek word for lizard.

Erlikosaurus was named and described by Barsbold and Perle in 1980. Fossils of Erlikosaurus were discovered in the Bayan Shireh Formation of Mongolia in 1972. The holotype specimen of Erlikosaurus was found at the Bayshin Tsav locality within the Bayan Shireh Formation. The Erlikosaurus fossils were found during a Soviet-Mongolian expedition in the Ömnögovi Province in 1972.

Erlikosaurus likely used a leaf-stripping feeding method involving active beak use aided by its neck. Differences between Erlikosaurus and the co-existing Segnosaurus suggest they occupied different ecological niches. Gregory S. Paul hypothesized that the long, slender claws of Erlikosaurus were used for self-defense. Therizinosaurs like Erlikosaurus were theropods that ate plants and possessed a backward-facing pubis similar to ornithischians.

Perle originally assigned Erlikosaurus to the Segnosauridae, a group now known as Therizinosauridae, a classification confirmed by later cladistic analyses. Erlikosaurus belongs to the parent group Therizinosauria. Erlikosaurus is classified within the class Reptilia.

Erlikosaurus lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period. Erlikosaurus lived approximately 96 to 89 million years ago. The Bayan Shireh Formation, where Erlikosaurus was found, dates from approximately 95.9 to 89.6 million years ago (Cenomanian to Santonian stages). Sediment analysis indicates Erlikosaurus lived in a semi-arid climate featuring wet environments with large meandering rivers and lakes.

In 2010, Gregory S. Paul suggested that Erlikosaurus might be synonymous with Enigmosaurus, a hypothesis disputed by Rinchen Barsbold. Most paleontologists currently consider Enigmosaurus and Erlikosaurus to be separate genera. In 1970, Rozhdestvensky proposed that therizinosaurs were theropods rather than non-dinosaur creatures, a view that was debated before being widely accepted.
